page: Vultr vhf-4c-16gb is a virtual server belonging to the High Frequency Compute family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture using an Intel processor configured with 4 vCPUs, which map to 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz under a shared allocation model. The hardware configuration includes 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and a bundled 384 GB NVMe SSD for local storage.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across primary compute metrics, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2411.16 and a multi-core score of 8740.87. The PassMark CPU score is 7697.28. However, the system exhibits performance limitations in memory-intensive tasks; large-block uncached memory bandwidth is weak, measuring 35.47 GB/sec for reads and 17.49 GB/sec for writes. Redis SET operations perform at an average rate of 6.0 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput is lower at 5.46 GB/sec.

This server represents a qualitatively cost-efficient profile for workloads requiring a balance of compute and fast local storage without the premium of dedicated CPU resources. The shared CPU allocation and moderate memory bandwidth make it less suitable for high-throughput data streaming or intensive multi-threaded compilation. It is best utilized for general-purpose applications, caching layers, and moderate database operations.
